content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.23), especially in early 30d horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative and recent prices are trending upward.
- Overshoot in 30d forecasts after sharp price increases (e.g., >80.5) — model tends to overreact.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after 3-5 consecutive days above 80.0.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3-5 days ago, model should adjust downward slightly in 30d forecast.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — reduce forecast spread or add 5-10% downward buffer if sentiment < 0.15.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2-3% to avoid momentum overfitting.
